name: Smoked Haddock, Sweetcorn & Coconut
desc: A smooth crossover between chowder and coconut fish soup.
ing: 220 g cooked smoked haddock, skin removed
method: Add haddock, sweetcorn, onion, garlic, ginger, stock and water.
Run Smooth.
Add coconut milk and black pepper.
Blend briefly; add only a background touch of lime if needed.
science: Haddock supplies lean protein and seafood micronutrients; sweetcorn contributes carotenoids.
note: Use cooked smoked haddock. Keep acidity quiet.

name: Prawn, Tomato, Saffron & Chilli Bisque
desc: A punchy, restaurant-style seafood soup with proper prawn flavour.
method: Add prawns, tomatoes, pepper, onion, garlic, stock, water, saffron, paprika and chilli.
Run Smooth.
Add cream.
Blend briefly and season.
science: Prawns are protein-dense; tomato and pepper add carotenoids and vitamin C.
note: Keep it seafood-forward rather than tomato-dominant.

name: Crab, Roasted Red Pepper & Parmesan Bisque
desc: Sweet crab pulled back towards savoury with Parmesan, garlic and pepper.
method: Add crab, pepper, tomatoes, onion, garlic, stock, water, paprika and cayenne.
Run Smooth.
Add Parmesan and cream.
Blend briefly until silky.
science: Crab brings protein, vitamin B12 and seafood minerals.
note: White and brown crab meat together give a deeper result.

name: Salmon, Spinach & Dill Crème Fraîche
desc: Rich salmon with spinach, dill and crème fraîche — essentially a potato-free fish-pie flavour profile.
method: Add salmon, spinach, cauliflower, onion, garlic, stock, dill and water.
Run Smooth.
Add crème fraîche and black pepper.
Blend briefly until silky.
science: Salmon supplies protein and EPA/DHA omega-3; spinach contributes carotenoids; cauliflower adds body without potato.
note: Hot-smoked salmon gives the strongest flavour with the least fuss.

name: Mackerel, Tomato & Smoked Paprika
desc: Oily mackerel meets a dark tomato-and-pepper base with garlic and smoked paprika.
method: Add mackerel, tomatoes, pepper, onion, garlic, paprika, chilli and water.
Run Smooth.
Taste, add black pepper, then Blend briefly if needed.
science: Mackerel is rich in protein and long-chain omega-3 fats; tomato and pepper add carotenoids.
note: Use mackerel in spring water, brine or oil according to preference; drain excess oil if very rich.

name: Tuna, Tomato, Olive & Parmesan
desc: A Mediterranean-style smooth tuna soup with black olives, garlic and Parmesan for maximum savouriness.
method: Add tuna, tomatoes, olives, onion, garlic, oregano and water.
Run Smooth.
Add Parmesan and black pepper.
Blend briefly and taste before adding salt.
science: Tuna provides a large amount of lean protein; olives and Parmesan bring fat and savoury depth.
note: Choose tuna in spring water or olive oil; both work, but oil-packed tuna makes a richer soup.

name: Cream of Crab
desc: A Maryland-inspired creamy crab soup adapted for a smooth 1 L batch.
method: Add 200 g crab meat, ½ onion, 100 g sweetcorn, 1 fish stock cube, 380 ml water and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 80 ml double cream, 1 tbsp dry sherry, pinch of mace, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Crab provides protein, vitamin B12 and minerals; this is deliberately rich rather than austere.
note: Brown crab meat adds excellent depth if your supermarket pack contains both white and brown meat.

name: Crab, Sweetcorn & Miso Cream
desc: Sweet crab and corn pulled firmly into savoury territory with white miso.
method: Add 200 g crab meat, 220 g sweetcorn, ½ onion, 3 garlic cloves and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 20 g white miso, 50 ml double cream, white or black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Crab supplies protein and B12; sweetcorn adds carotenoids while miso boosts savouriness.
note: Keep the miso moderate so crab remains the main flavour.

name: Salmon, Miso & Spinach Cream
desc: Rich salmon and spinach with miso and garlic instead of a conventional cream-sauce profile.
method: Add 220 g cooked or hot-smoked salmon, 100 g baby spinach, 150 g cauliflower, ½ onion, 3 garlic cloves and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 20 g white miso, 50 ml double cream, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Salmon supplies protein and EPA/DHA omega-3; spinach contributes folate and carotenoids.
note: Hot-smoked salmon gives the strongest flavour.

name: Prawn, Tomato & Saffron Coconut Cream
desc: Prawns, tomato, saffron and coconut: halfway between bisque and coconut curry.
method: Add 220 g cooked prawns, 300 g chopped tomatoes, 140 g roasted red pepper, ½ onion, 3 garlic cloves, small pinch saffron, ½ tsp smoked paprika and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 120 ml light coconut milk, black pepper, pinch of chilli.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Prawns provide lean protein; tomato and pepper contribute carotenoids and vitamin C.
note: Saffron is optional but makes this feel much more luxurious.

name: Thai Coconut Prawn & Lemongrass
desc: A smooth, coriander-free coconut prawn soup with lemongrass, ginger and medium chilli.
ing: 1 lemongrass stalk, tender inner part finely sliced
method: Add 220 g cooked prawns, 1 lemongrass stalk, 10 g ginger, 3 garlic cloves, ½ onion, 1 fish stock cube and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 150 ml light coconut milk, 1 tsp lime juice, chilli to taste, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Prawns provide protein; the rest of the recipe is built for aromatic flavour rather than health claims.
note: Keep lime in the background, as requested.

name: Sardine, Garlic, Fennel & Tomato
desc: A Sicilian-leaning sardine soup with fennel, tomato and a lot of garlic.
method: Add 1 tin sardines, 350 g chopped tomatoes, 130 g fennel bulb, ½ onion, 4 garlic cloves, ½ tsp dried oregano and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 25 g parmesan, black pepper, pinch of chilli.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Sardines supply protein, EPA/DHA, B12 and calcium when the soft bones are eaten.
note: One tin is plenty for a 1 L smooth batch.

name: Sardine, Tomato, Chilli & Mascarpone
desc: Bold sardine and tomato rounded off by mascarpone and a medium chilli warmth.
ing: Pinch to ½ tsp chilli flakes
method: Add 1 tin sardines, 380 g chopped tomatoes, 120 g roasted red pepper, ½ onion, 4 garlic cloves, pinch to ½ tsp chilli flakes and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 60 g mascarpone, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Sardines are a concentrated source of protein and long-chain omega-3 fats.
note: Mascarpone softens the fishiness without hiding it.

name: Sardine, Sweetcorn & Smoked Paprika Cream
desc: Sweetcorn balances oily sardine while smoked paprika makes the whole thing feel deliberate.
method: Add 1 tin sardines, 260 g sweetcorn, ½ onion, 3 garlic cloves, ½ tsp smoked paprika, 1 vegetable stock cube and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 50 ml double cream, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Sardines bring protein and omega-3; corn provides fibre and carotenoids.
note: A strong wildcard flavour-wise, but very supermarket-friendly.

name: Sardine, Mushroom & Miso
desc: Aggressively umami in the best way: sardine, mushroom, miso and garlic.
method: Add 1 tin sardines, 240 g chestnut mushrooms, ½ onion, 4 garlic cloves, 10 g ginger and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 18 g white or awase miso, 1 tsp light soy sauce, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Sardine, mushroom and miso each provide different savoury compounds, producing a very deep flavour profile.
note: Do not add extra salt before tasting.

name: Smoked Haddock, Sweetcorn & Cream
desc: The straightforward creamy version of one of your strongest flavour combinations.
method: Add 220 g cooked smoked haddock, 220 g sweetcorn, ½ onion, 3 garlic cloves, 1 fish or chicken stock cube and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 70 ml double cream, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Haddock provides lean protein; sweetcorn adds carotenoids and body without potato.
note: Simple on purpose: smoked haddock should dominate.

name: Mussel, Tomato & Saffron Bisque
desc: Strong shellfish flavour with tomato, saffron, garlic and cream.
method: Add 220 g cooked mussel meat, 320 g chopped tomatoes, 150 g roasted red pepper, ½ onion, 4 garlic cloves, small pinch saffron, 1 fish stock cube and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 60 ml double cream, black pepper, pinch of cayenne.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Mussels provide protein, iron, B12 and other seafood micronutrients.
note: Use cooked shelled mussels; frozen is perfectly sensible.

name: Cod, Leek & Roasted-Garlic Cream
desc: Clean white fish, leek and lots of garlic in a smooth, pale cream.
method: Add 240 g cooked cod, 220 g leek, 150 g cauliflower, 4 garlic cloves, 1 fish stock cube and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 60 ml double cream, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Cod is very lean and protein-rich; cauliflower gives body while leek adds sweetness.
note: Use cooked cod or another cooked firm white fish.

name: Anchovy, Tomato & Parmesan Garlic Soup
desc: Anchovy promoted from seasoning to co-star, but balanced by tomato, garlic and Parmesan.
method: Add 8 anchovy fillets, 400 g chopped tomatoes, 150 g roasted red pepper, ½ onion, 4 garlic cloves and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 30 g parmesan, 50 ml double cream, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Anchovies provide protein, omega-3 fats and calcium; their intensity means a small quantity flavours the whole batch.
note: Do not salt before tasting.

name: Smoked Trout, Sweetcorn & Crème Fraîche
desc: Smoked trout with corn, dill and crème fraîche: creamy, smoky and slightly fresher than haddock.
method: Add 210 g smoked trout, 200 g sweetcorn, ½ onion, 3 garlic cloves, ½ tsp dried dill, 1 fish stock cube and the stated liquid to the jug, keeping below the MAX line.
Run the Smooth programme.
Add 60 g crème fraîche, black pepper.
Blend briefly until the texture is completely smooth, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
science: Trout supplies complete protein and omega-3 fats; corn contributes carotenoids.
note: Smoked trout varies in saltiness, so season at the end.
